newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's Peters rejoins coalition talks.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's Peters rejoins coalition talks.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters turned up for Thursday's fourth round of talks with the caretaker conservative National Party team, after missing Wednesday's talks with both National and the main opposition Labour Party.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger had minutes before told journalists he did not expect Peters to be there.
"We were told yesterday he wouldn't be there today," Bolger said.

The economic nationalist New Zealand First party holds the balance of power after the inconclusive general election on October 12, and is negotiating with both National and Labour over the shape of the new government.
Talks are expected to last several weeks and Peters has not indicated which way he is leaning.

Peters on Wednesday downplayed reports of early morning scuffles with patrons at the opening of a Wellington bar and restaurant, and the presence there of Mike Moore -- one of the senior negotiators in Labour's team.
Peters told the Dominion newspaper Moore and he had been having coalition-related talks at the bar, and similar discussions were going on with National party negotiators outside the formal sessions.
Bolger on Thursday confirmed informal talks were taking place.
"There is a lot of informal contact, from meetings in (parliament's) Bellamy's dining room to everything else. I know of none at 3 a.m. in the morning," Bolger said.
Peters would not comment on the talks as he went into Thursday's meeting with National.
New Zealand First is scheduled to meet Labour again on Thursday afternoon at 2 p.m. (0100 GMT)
